P2.mechanism: advisory (cooperative); expected to fail condition (b) by construction, which is the point of the probe

evidence.reason: The filesystem has no state it recognizes as an uncommitted effect. A staged file is an ordinary visible file; that it is 'pending' is a naming convention of the writer and reader, and nothing binds it to an authority object that revocation acts on (contrast pg_prepared_xacts, or an etcd key bound to a lease). Staged-then-rename gives an atomic commit-versus-unlink race via rename(2), which a cooperative shim can use, but that is a protocol built on the filesystem, in the same way a hold can be built on any store, so E6 does not count it as a filesystem primitive.

documentation.headline: Amazon S3 now supports conditional writes
documentation.quote: To use conditional writes, you can add the HTTP if-none-match conditional header along with PutObject and CompleteMultipartUpload API requests.

documentation.headline: Amazon S3 adds new functionality for conditional writes
documentation.quote: S3 then evaluates if the object's ETag matches the value provided in the API request before committing the write and prevents your clients from overwriting the object until the condition is satisfied.

quotes: The If-None-Match header prevents overwrites of existing data by validating that there's not an object with the same key name already in your bucket.
If the ETag doesn't match, the write operation fails with a 412 Precondition Failed response.
Bucket owners can use bucket policies to enforce conditional writes for uploaded objects.
This operation aborts a multipart upload.
After a multipart upload is aborted, no additional parts can be uploaded using that upload ID.

evidence.mechanism: If-None-Match: * on PutObject / CompleteMultipartUpload (create-once by key; 412 if the key exists)

evidence.analysis_not_documentation: The precondition is per object. A fence floor kept in a separate object cannot be checked atomically with writing the effect object, so an epoch fence needs the floor and the effect in the same object (or a sink in front of S3). The If-Match header must be supplied by the writer; bucket policies can require the conditional headers to be present but do not supply a floor.
Abort cancels an upload in progress. Crash durability of an in-progress multipart upload was not tested; the hold covers object creation only.
